heading: Pick the one for your computer.
intro: Celadon {{version}}, released {{date}}. Two Mac installers split by chip, one for Windows; after installing, rescan plug-ins in your host.
introStale: Celadon {{version}}: two Mac installers split by chip, one for Windows.

mac-arm64.system: M1 and later · macOS 12 or later
mac-arm64.how: Apple menu → About This Mac: the Chip line says Apple M…

mac-x64.how: About This Mac lists an Intel Processor. Also use this one for hosts running under Rosetta on an Apple silicon Mac.

win-x64.how: Windows 11 is always 64-bit; on Windows 10, check System type under Settings → System → About.

stale.title: The installers haven't been updated to {{version}} yet.
stale.body: Until the new installers are up, older files aren't offered here, so nobody installs the wrong one. To see what's changed in this version:

firstLaunch.title: The system will stop it once — allow it and you're done.
firstLaunch.body: The installers carry no Apple Developer ID signature and no Windows code signature, so the system blocks them the first time. Allow them as shown below; there's no need to turn off any security settings.

macSteps: Double-click the .pkg. When the system says it can't be opened, dismiss the alert — don't click <ui>Move to Trash</ui>.

Open <ui>System Settings → Privacy & Security</ui>, scroll down to the Celadon entry, click <ui>Open Anyway</ui> and enter your password. On macOS 12 it's under <ui>System Preferences → Security & Privacy</ui>.
In the installer, click <ui>Customize</ui> to install only the formats you need: VST3, AU or the standalone app.
winSteps: Double-click the .exe and you'll see <ui>Windows protected your PC</ui>.

On the wizard's <ui>Components</ui> page, VST3 and the standalone app are both ticked by default. Clear either one; clearing both stops the wizard. The standalone app appears as Celadon in the Start menu.

after.rescan: Rescan plug-ins in your host; Logic validates AUs automatically. If the host has been open all along, save your project and restart it once so it doesn't keep using the old version.
after.twice: If you've built it yourself in Xcode and it sits in your personal plug-in folder ~/Library/Audio/Plug-Ins/, don't run the installer as well — your host would show two copies of Celadon.
after.verify: Optional. On a Mac, run shasum -a 256 file in Terminal; on Windows, run Get-FileHash file in PowerShell. If the result matches the SHA-256 on the card (case doesn't matter), the file is intact. All three checksums are also in a single {{file}} file.
after.uninstall: On Windows, uninstall from Settings → Apps. On a Mac, delete Celadon from Components and VST3 under /Library/Audio/Plug-Ins/, and Celadon from Applications.

requirements: Celadon needs macOS 12 or later (Apple silicon or Intel), or 64-bit Windows 10 / 11.

notice.macTitle: Looks like a Mac, but this browser doesn't say which chip.
notice.macBody: Apple menu → <ui>About This Mac</ui>: if the <ui>Chip</ui> line says Apple M…, pick Apple silicon; if it lists an Intel <ui>Processor</ui>, pick Intel.
notice.winArmBody: The installer is x64: it needs Windows 11 (which runs it through emulation), and only x64 hosts can load it — native ARM hosts can't.
notice.unsupportedTail: You can still download the installers below and move them to your computer.

started.body: {{file}}, {{size}} MB. If it didn't start, click here. The system will stop it once when you install — allow it as shown below.

unsupported.phone: Looks like you're on a phone. Celadon is an audio plug-in for computers — install it on a Mac or Windows PC.
unsupported.tablet: Looks like you're on a tablet. Celadon is an audio plug-in for computers — install it on a Mac or Windows PC.
unsupported.linux: Looks like you're on Linux. Celadon is available for Mac and Windows only for now.
unsupported.chromeos: Looks like you're on ChromeOS. Celadon is available for Mac and Windows only for now.
unsupported.old-windows: Looks like Windows 7 / 8. Celadon needs Windows 10 or 11 (64-bit).
unsupported.windows-32: Looks like 32-bit Windows. Celadon is 64-bit only.
unsupported.old-macos: Looks like this Mac is running something older than macOS 12. Celadon needs macOS 12 (Monterey) or later.
